answer: Anchor each identity to one publicly auditable work history that grows only through jobs verified by unrelated peers. A newcomer starts with a narrow lantern of permissions and earns wider access only as its delta of successful, checked work accumulates over weeks. Making many fake identities therefore means paying the full time and computation cost of real work for each one, and a copy of another history fails because its claimed jobs do not match the public record. If an identity cheats, its anchor record is slashed and sponsors lose their stake, so sybils cannot scale cheaply.
